A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TAAT research work. All nine pages of each version were inspected through text extraction and rendering, including equations, figures, tables, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; no material gaps limit comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original TAAT motion-generation results in Tables 2–4, a 20-participant dataset-validation study in Section 3, and action-label accuracy results in Section 5.2 and Figure 6.

after.justification: v2 retains the original TAAT benchmark results, dataset-validation study, and action-label accuracy analysis reported in v1.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same LLM action-label extraction, VQ-VAE representation, Transformer generation, and procedure for joining successive actions. No algorithm, architecture, objective, or inference step changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use HumanML3D and HumanML3D++ for action-text and scene-text motion generation, including the same generalization scenario from HumanML3D training to HumanML3D++ testing.

E2.justification: Tables 2–4 retain the same comparator membership: TM2T, MDM, MLD, MotionDiffuse, and T2M-GPT. The comparison methods displayed in the figures are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 3 and 5 retain identical validation sampling, training/testing arrangements, model configurations, budgets, feature-extractor procedures, and evaluation metrics. The ten-candidate action-selection procedure in Section 5.2 is unchanged.

E4.justification: The scene-text generalization evaluation, Text2Action accuracy analysis in Section 5.2 and Figure 6, and qualitative examples in Figure 4 are unchanged. No ablation or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Tables 2–4 retain identical ± reporting. Neither version adds or revises repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty-estimation explanations, confidence levels, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, TAAT FID remains 0.461, 0.488, and 0.448 in Tables 2, 3, and 4, respectively; Figure 6 retains the 18% match, 48% similar, and 34% mismatch breakdown.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 retains identical mathematical definitions, quantization and loss equations, autoregressive formulation, and action-conditioning rule in Equations 1–5. No assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about arbitrary-text motion generation, HumanML3D++, the two-stage framework, and improved understanding of scene texts.

C2.justification: The interpretations of generalization and motion quality are identical. Sections 5.2 and 6 retain the same qualifications about LLM randomness, multiple reasonable responses to a scene, and limitations of existing evaluation metrics.

D1.justification: The dataset-generation prompts, filtering instructions, implementation settings, optimization schedules, and evaluation details are unchanged. Both abstracts retain the same statement that the dataset and code will be released.

R1.justification: Section 2, the research-positioning passages elsewhere, and all 40 reference entries are identical. No cited work or relationship to prior research changes.

P1.justification: v2 changes 'GuoPeng Li' to 'Guopeng Li' in the author list and running headers and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. All remaining text and section organization are identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–6, Tables 1–4, equations, captions, and page layout are unchanged. Rendered differences are confined to the author text and arXiv stamp, with no figure, table, or layout revision.

improvement.justification: v2 changes only author-name capitalization and the arXiv version/date stamp. The methods, empirical evidence, explanations, limitations, reproducibility information, and visual organization remain identical, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
